What's the best life advice you've ever gotten.

My dad always tells me to be consistent. Not practice harder, read more, be indispensable; but be consistent. If you have a goal that your working towards, and your consistent at working towards that goal every day for a week, month, year, decade - you WILL become the best there is in that field. I'm constantly jumping from project to project, hobby to hobby, etc. etc., and they never work out, I never get good because my focus is too spread out. Most people who are working towards a goal and continue to see failure just need to be more consistent.

Was dating a guy who I genuinely loved, but he was a stoner working a dead-end job with no ambitions in life, and I was a college-student driving home on the weekends to stay with him. At a family party, his sister-in-law pulled me aside and said something along the lines of, "Look, I know what you're thinking. You're thinking that you really love this guy, and he's great, and that you'll get him to change. He'll stop drinking, stop smoking, and get a better job. You'll be able to pull him out of this. But that's not the case. What will happen is that you'll drop out of college, you'll get married, you'll have a few kids, and you'll look at him one day and realize you sacrificed everything for this guy who never changed. I know, because I was you, and I did that, and I'm miserable. So I love you, and I really want you to be part of this family, but don't. Just leave." Then she hugged me and told me that she hoped she never saw me again.

It forced me to step outside of my feelings and really look at the situation. She was right. We broke up a few weeks later, and 10-years later he's still a stoner, still working a crap job, still living with his boys, etc.

I saw her a few years later. She was a coach for my niece's gymnastics team. She just smiled and nodded to me. Best advice I ever got.
